plan: In a symmetric, independent private-values second-price auction, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value: you win exactly when it’s profitable and pay the second-highest bid. With no history to infer systematic over/underbidding by others, deviating risks either overpaying or missing profitable wins. Bid exactly 42.

[ Second-price sealed-bid with independent private values: the weakly dominant strategy is truthful bidding. With three bidders and uniform values 0–49, bidding your value maximizes expected profit; shading only increases the chance of losing when you’d profit, and overbidding risks losses. Ties are random but do not change optimality. One round, no history to exploit. Therefore, bid exactly my value: 29. ]

[ This is a sealed-bid, second-price auction with three bidders. The dominant strategy is to bid my true private value to maximize expected profit regardless of others’ bids. Underbidding risks losing when I should win; overbidding doesn’t increase the price paid but risks inefficient wins. With value $48 and one round (no learning), bidding $48 ensures I win whenever the second-highest bid is at most 48 and pay that amount. ]
